All 6 ACs covered (AC-1..AC-6), 15 total test cases, numbering matches the AC matrix at the end. The test spec is complete.

**Report:**

Wrote `aiws/work/REQ-006/03-test-spec.md` (only file touched, within write scope).

- **14 test cases total**: TC-117, TC-118, TC-120, TC-122, TC-127 redefined (keep code, display name, data rows, run counts — per the TC-92/97/105 precedent from REQ-004, not the TC-36/74 "note only" precedent, since AC-5/AC-6 need a TC and mã TC lives in the display name); TC-135..TC-144 new, numbered from TC-135 as `conventions.md` requires.
- **AC coverage**: AC-1→TC-135/136, AC-2→TC-138/139/142, AC-3→TC-137/140/141, AC-4→TC-143/144, AC-5→TC-117/118/120/122, AC-6→TC-127. Every AC has ≥1 TC (`every_ac_has_tc`).
- TCs are split by *kind* of expected result, not by concrete value (per the unit-testing skill): e.g. `chooseStatusClickKey` alone splits into "returns given id" (TC-137) vs "returns shared non-string key" (TC-138); the guard-integration behaviors split into "rejected within window" (TC-139), "accepted from 500ms, anchor doesn't move on a rejected click" (TC-140), "Tất cả stays per-customer" (TC-141), and the out-of-AC-premise filter-switch cases (TC-142, flagged as "D4/Q3, ngoài tiền đề của AC" per D10's suggestion).
- Each new FE unit maps to real data/row values pulled from the design's own tables (D1, D3, D5), and the five redefined BE/FE tests' expected-result blocks spell out exactly which assertions are old (unchanged, verbatim) vs. new (D7/D8/D9), since part (a) of AC-5/AC-6 is only checkable by diff review (R6) — flagged explicitly.
- Added the usual supporting sections: variant→TC/manual-step mapping (since `index.html`/`main.js` wiring has no automated test), "Kỳ vọng phụ thuộc quyết định đang chờ duyệt" tied to design's open decisions, TC→file→task-group table, expected counts (BE unchanged at 399; FE 53→63), and "Chưa chạy kiểm chứng" predictions.

Reviewer should know: FE count math (53 + 2 + 6 + 2 = 63) and the BE run-count claims (173/107/399) depend on the design's stated baselines, not on anything I ran — no tests were executed in this phase.
